question: Inside each layer of `src/vs`, code is split into folders by the environment it runs in. What are those environments, and what may code in each one import?

points.text: `browser` (web APIs such as the DOM; may use `common`)
`electron-browser` (browser APIs plus a small IPC subset to the Electron main process; may use `common` and `browser`)

answer:
Within each layer of `src/vs`, code is split into folders by runtime environment. This comes from `.github/instructions/source-code-organization.instructions.md`, which I read. I didn't check it against actual imports in the code.

| Folder | Runs in / APIs available | May import from |
|---|---|---|
| `common` | Plain JavaScript only, with no DOM and no Node | `common` only |
| `browser` | Web/DOM APIs | `common` |
| `node` | Node.js APIs | `common` |
| `electron-browser` | The renderer: browser APIs plus limited Electron IPC | `common`, `browser` |
| `electron-utility` | The Electron utility process | `common`, `node` |
| `electron-main` | The Electron main process | `common`, `node`, `electron-utility` |

Two rules apply on top of the environment split:

- **Layers.** Each layer can only import from layers below it. The order from bottom to top is `base`, `platform`, `editor`, `workbench`, then `code` and `server` (the desktop and remote-server entry points). `sessions` (the Agent Sessions window) can import from `workbench` and below, but `workbench` must never import from `sessions`.
- **Editor layer.** `editor` must not depend on `node` or `electron-*` code.

The workbench also has a few rules of its own:

- Its minimal core lives in `common`, `browser` and `electron-browser`.
- Anything outside `contrib/` must not import from inside it.
- Each contribution has a single `.contribution.ts` entry point.
